\subsection{Electrochemical Models}\label{ss:analog-models}

Every measurement in this chapter that involves an electrode uses one of two lumped
models from the \texttt{castalia} library, drawn in Figures~\ref{fig:randles-cell}
and~\ref{fig:randles-electrode}, with values in Table~\ref{tab:analog-models}. They are stated once here and referenced by the
block sections rather than repeated, because the electrode impedance is not a detail of
the setup: it sets the feedback factor of the potentiostat loop and of the
transimpedance loop, and both blocks' stability figures depend on it directly.

\texttt{randles\_cell} is the three-electrode arrangement the potentiostat actually
drives. Looking into the working electrode it presents \(R_{\mathrm{ct}} \parallel
C_{\mathrm{dl}}\) in series with \(R_u\): about \SI{31}{\kilo\ohm} at DC, falling toward
\(R_u = \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}\) as \(C_{\mathrm{dl}}\) shorts the charge-transfer branch
above roughly \SI{5}{\hertz}. \texttt{randles\_electrode} is a single interface as a
two-terminal element, with a much smaller double layer and a much larger charge-transfer
resistance; it is not used by the benches reported here.

\begin{table}[htbp]
  \centering
  \caption[{Component values of the electrochemical models.}]{Component values of the
  electrochemical models of Figures~\ref{fig:randles-cell} and~\ref{fig:randles-electrode}. The \texttt{randles\_cell}
  values are the subcircuit defaults, and are the values the control-amplifier
  benches instantiate. The transimpedance benches override them; the values used are
  stated with each measurement.}
  \label{tab:analog-models}
  \begin{tabular}{llrl}
    \toprule
    Model & Element & Value & Represents \\
    \midrule
    \texttt{randles\_cell}      & $R_{\mathrm{ce}}$  & \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}    & solution resistance, CE to RE \\
                                & $R_u$              & \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}    & uncompensated resistance, RE to WE surface \\
                                & $R_{\mathrm{ct}}$  & \SI{30}{\kilo\ohm}   & charge transfer at the WE interface \\
                                & $C_{\mathrm{dl}}$  & \SI{1}{\micro\farad} & double layer at the WE interface \\
    \addlinespace
    \texttt{randles\_electrode} & $R_s$              & \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}   & series solution resistance \\
                                & $R_{\mathrm{ct}}$  & \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}    & charge transfer \\
                                & $C_{\mathrm{dl}}$  & \SI{10}{\nano\farad} & double layer \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

Two limits apply to every number derived through these models. Both are linear and
frequency-independent: there is no Warburg diffusion term and no potential dependence,
so they describe small-signal behaviour about a bias point, not a full electrochemical
response. And they are nominal: no spread is assigned to any element, so no result in
this chapter accounts for electrode-to-electrode variation, which on a real wound
interface is likely to exceed the process spread reported alongside it.

\paragraph{Values used by the amplifier application benches.} The closed-loop measurements of Section~\ref{ss:ampab} instantiate \texttt{randles\_cell} with $R_u = \SI{100}{\ohm}$ or \SI{1}{\kilo\ohm}, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ or \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}, and $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$ or \SI{1}{\micro\farad}, in place of the subcircuit defaults above. The value used is stated with each measurement.
